chunks: I praise Allah for whatever matter He ordained and whatever action He destines, and for my trial with you, O group
who do not obey when I order and do not respond when I call you.
If you are at ease you engage in (conceited) conversation, but if you are faced with battle you show weakness.
If people agree on one Imam you taunt each other.
If you are faced with an arduous matter you turn away from it.
May others have no father (woe to your enemy!) what are you waiting for, in the matter of your assistance and for fighting for your rights?
For you there is either death or disgrace.
By Allah, if my day (of death) comes, and it is sure to come, it will cause separation between me and you, although I am sick of your company,
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the disobedient companions mentioned in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha captures the climax of Imam Ali’s patience with the Khawarij, whom he characterizes as a faction defined by inconsistency—acting rashly when given respite but fleeing when combat is joined. The rhetorical question 'What do you wait for?' underscores the imminent shift from political tolerance to decisive military confrontation, marking the transition from the era of internal dissent to the Battle of Nahrawan. This critique highlights the Shia scholarly view that their disobedience was not merely tactical but a fundamental deviation from the Imam’s authority.
